key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that MgSiO3 post-perovskite conducts lattice heat 44–55% better than bridgmanite at matching lower-mantle pressures and temperatures.
engineering_relevance: The resulting conductivity parameterizations support lower-mantle thermal models, with predicted core–mantle boundary aggregate conductivities encompassing the commonly assumed 10 W/(m K).
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Calculate the quasi-harmonic phase boundary and estimate aggregate conductivity using Hashin–Shtrikman bounds.
evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, substituting DFT for MACE forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes lattice conductivity by only 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
watch_item: The aggregate estimates describe Fe-free end members; composition and microstructure effects require further assessment before application to the real mantle.
paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
